title: Ranveer Singh Is About to Destroy Mumbai — and Spend ₹300 Crore Doing It
excerpt: India's first post-apocalyptic zombie thriller begins filming in Australia this September. Kalyani Priyadarshan makes her Bollywood debut. And Ranveer personally called to make it happen.
body:
There are certain things Bollywood has never seriously attempted. A proper zombie apocalypse — with the budget to match, the VFX to sell it, and a star who can carry a devastated world on his back — has been somewhere near the top of that list. **Ranveer Singh** just crossed it off.

**Pralay**, a ₹300-crore post-apocalyptic thriller directed by **Jai Mehta**, is officially in motion. Filming begins in **September 2026** across Australia, with pre-production already underway and international technicians building a devastated, dystopian version of Mumbai that has no precedent in Indian cinema. This is the most expensive original concept the industry has ever greenlit.

## The Gamble After the Glory

Ranveer's last two films — **Dhurandhar** (₹1,200+ crore worldwide) and **Dhurandhar 2** (₹1,375 crore) — have made him, by the numbers, the most bankable star in Indian cinema right now. Most actors would play it safe after that kind of run. Sign a sequel. Do the prestige biopic. Coast on goodwill.

Ranveer chose zombies.

Under his newly launched production banner, **Maa Kasam Films** — yes, that's the actual name, and it's somehow perfect for him — Singh is co-producing *Pralay* with **Hansal Mehta's True Story Films** and **Applause Entertainment**. It's his debut as a producer, and the first project he's putting his own money behind is a genre Indian audiences have never supported at anything close to this scale.

The film is described as a survival story about a married couple fighting to stay alive in a zombie-ravaged Mumbai. Large-scale action meets emotional storytelling, with AI-driven visuals and cutting-edge VFX shaping a dystopian world designed to compete globally.

## Jai Mehta: The Name You Should Know

Director **Jai Mehta** — Hansal's son, co-director of *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story*, and the force behind the streaming thriller *Lootere* — has been developing the screenplay with co-writer **Vishal Kapoor**. When rumours surfaced that *Pralay* was an adaptation of José Saramago's *Blindness*, Hansal himself stepped in to shut them down.

> "This is an original story. A novel like *Blindness* is not easily adapted to film." — Hansal Mehta

The project carries an interesting father-son symmetry: Hansal producing while Jai directs, much like the Hirani dynamic playing out across town with *Pritam and Pedro*. Bollywood's next generation isn't waiting for permission. They're building their own universes.

## The Call That Changed the Cast

Then there's **Kalyani Priyadarshan** — daughter of filmmaker **Priyadarshan**, a growing force in Malayalam and Telugu cinema, and the star of the blockbuster fantasy thriller *Lokah: Chapter 1 – Chandra*. She's making her Bollywood debut as Ranveer's on-screen wife.

She was reportedly hesitant. A post-apocalyptic zombie thriller isn't the safe Bollywood entry point — no Dharma rom-com, no wholesome family drama. But Ranveer, operating as both leading man and producer, personally called her. He walked her through the script's vision, the scale of the Australian production, and why her particular intensity was essential to the character.

She said yes.

The pairing makes instinctive sense. Ranveer is volcanic — all detonation and adrenaline. Kalyani is precise, coiled, capable of an emotional depth that doesn't need volume. In a film about a marriage tested by the literal end of the world, that contrast could be electric.

## Why the Diaspora Should Be Watching

*Pralay* is being filmed in **Australia** — home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities — and the VFX-heavy, globally-scaled production signals ambitions that stretch well beyond the domestic box office. For NRI audiences who've spent years asking when Indian cinema would take genre filmmaking as seriously as Hollywood or South Korea, this is Bollywood's clearest answer.

The budget. The talent. The location. The willingness to bet a fortune on something with zero precedent in Hindi cinema. *Pralay* is either going to be a watershed moment for Indian genre filmmaking or the most spectacular gamble this industry has ever seen.

Filming begins September 2026. If Ranveer's recent track record is anything to go by, the zombies should be worried.
